bulging_tunnel.capacity: FEEL how parametric distortion transforms a predictable corridor into an unpredictable cave
bulging_tunnel.description: Walk into a cylinder that refuses to stay regular. CSG spheres bulge outward at irregular intervals, warping your sense of depth — the tunnel breathes. The num_bulges and bulge_max_radius parameters control how much chaos enters the geometry: low values produce a hallway, high values produce a cave. Contrasts with Klein bottle (closed non-orientable) and Möbius strip (twisted surface); prepares for hyperbolic spaces where distortion becomes the rule.
interactions: change bulge_max_radius to control distortion intensity
toggle use_random_bulges for deterministic vs stochastic
bulging_tunnel.name: Bulging Tunnel

parameters.use_random_bulges: Stochastic vs sinusoidal bulge sizing (default: true)

bulging_tunnel.qfep_connection: Lambda applied to architecture — a regular cylinder is pure F (uniform, predictable). Each bulge introduces E (variation, surprise). The num_bulges parameter IS lambda: how much chaos do you let into your structure? At zero bulges the tunnel is Euclidean. At maximum, geometry becomes landscape.

curvature_slider.description: VR slider controlling Gaussian curvature from negative (hyperbolic) through zero (flat/Euclidean) to positive (elliptic). Emits curvature_changed signal for linked surfaces.
curvature_slider.name: Curvature Slider

elliptic_surface.description: Dome/sphere-like surface demonstrating positive Gaussian curvature (K > 0) — where parallel lines converge and triangle angles sum to more than 180 degrees.
elliptic_surface.name: Elliptic Surface

dna.default: found_state=stirred, level=minimal - both are pure no-ops. `stirred` falls through to `_:` and never assigns S, `minimal` never assigns threshold_center, so the scene's own S (0.3) and threshold (0.0) survive untouched. The 7 existing placements (Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis, _p1, _p2, _p3, Corridor_Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis, Morphogenesis_Intro, Curation_Bay_softbodies_4) render byte-identically to before.
dna.was: A gyroid at one entropy value with a full inspector of exports and apply_grid_config() = pass, so no map token could reach a single knob. found_state opens the S scale that was already the declared critical_parameter; level opens threshold_center, which the artifact's own truth line names and which had been nailed to 0.0 everywhere. field_seed is a fixture knob, not an axis: GyroidFieldGenerator does noise.seed = randi(), so unpinned the sweep would photograph five different gyroids.
dna.notes: framing 0.85 because the volume is 5x10x5 - fit-by-diagonal (12.2) pulls the camera back for an extent that is never wider than 5. `shelled` from entropy_jar's list is deliberately absent: there it is a joke about the jar's vertical binning, and this artifact carries no instrument to fool.

entropy_morphogenesis.description: A gyroid triply-periodic minimal surface built by marching cubes at one chosen entropy. S maps to frequency, noise amplitude and cut threshold together, so a single number decides whether the surface is a legible crystal or a crumpled labyrinth.
entropy_morphogenesis.name: entropy_morphogenesis

gyroid_cheese.name: gyroid_cheese
gyroid_cheese.qfep_connection: sin·cos summed three ways yields a surface with no rooms, only two interlocked corridors that never touch — and marching cubes plus a generated collision body commits that implicit equation to something your feet must negotiate.

hyperbolic_surface.description: Saddle-shaped surface demonstrating negative Gaussian curvature (K < 0) — where parallel lines diverge and triangle angles sum to less than 180 degrees.
hyperbolic_surface.name: Hyperbolic Surface

marching_cubes.description: Test scene for marching cubes algorithm verification with basic sphere and voxel tests
marching_cubes.name: Marching Cubes Test
marching_cubes.qfep_connection: The surface is a verdict: a continuous noise field, cut at a threshold, hardens into walkable terrain. The sliders move the field; the verdict itself never appears on any slider.

mobius_strip_altgeo.description: A walkable Möbius strip environment — traverse the one-sided surface and experience the topological twist firsthand. Non-orientability as lived experience.
mobius_strip_altgeo.name: Möbius Strip (Walkable)

mobius_world.description: Walkable MÃ¶bius strip - non-orientable surface. Requires MovementWallWalk on player (collision layer 4).
mobius_world.name: MÃ¶bius World

non_euclidean_space.description: A space where Euclid's parallel postulate fails — rooms that are bigger inside than outside, corridors that loop impossibly. Hyperbolic and elliptic geometry made navigable.
non_euclidean_space.name: Non-Euclidean Space
non_euclidean_space.qfep_connection: Euclid fails here not by curving space but by bookkeeping: portals stitch disjoint rooms so corridors loop and interiors exceed their shells, and the manager quietly signals each crossing. Consistency turns out to be a rendering convention your walking body can be talked out of.

dna.default: formation=chance, cast=all - reproduces the shipped build exactly. formation=chance calls the same coin flip at the same two thresholds the hard-coded expressions used (0.5 on the shell's deformation spheres, 0.3 on the tunnel details), and cast=all runs membranes, crystals and growths together as before, so all 13 existing placements are untouched.
dna.was: One hard-coded expression, twice: `OPERATION_UNION if randf() > 0.5 else OPERATION_SUBTRACTION` on the shell and the same at 0.3 on the tunnel details. The artifact's own truth line says organic form 'is what remains after noise has eaten away at geometry from within' — but the code was flipping a coin between eating away and piling on, and never said so. formation states the position; erode is the truth line taken literally, accrete is its opposite, alternate is neither chance nor doctrine but rhythm. cast was three generators that always all ran; the word and the all-plus-one-each shape are borrowed verbatim from particle_systems.cast, which asks the same question of its emitters.
dna.fixture_note: MANDATORY for the sweep. Every draw in this artifact was an unseeded global randf/randi, so without a pinned seed the N variants are N different caves and any bite number measures the RNG, not the axis (the trap CLAUDE.md names for generative artifacts). form_seed now routes all randomness through one RandomNumberGenerator; 0 keeps the shipped fresh-every-run behaviour, so this pin is capture-bench only and no placement sees it.
dna.framing_note: The subject is 25 m across (space_size 25,18,25 in the .tscn) and mostly hollow shell. If the sweep reports a small subject share, that is the shell's thin wall against a big frame, not an inert axis.

organic_space.description: An algorithmic exploration of organic geometries and natural forms, creating flowing, non-Euclidean spaces that challenge traditional geometric assumptions
organic_space.name: Organic Space
organic_space.qfep_connection: A space that looks grown rather than built — chambers and passages with the irregular rightness of something that developed instead of being placed. The proof that 'organic' is not a texture but a *process*: authorless form has a feel, and the walker can tell.

dna.fixture_why: MANDATORY for the sweep, and not an axis. The layout is drawn entirely from the UNSEEDED global randf/randi — generation_seed only ever fed the two FastNoiseLite fields, never the growth — so four topology frames would be four different mazes and any bite number would be measuring the RNG rather than the rule. This is the generative-artifact trap in CLAUDE.md. layout_draw defaults to `fresh`, which is the shipped every-launch-is-a-new-maze behaviour and is the artifact's point, so no placement ever sees the pin.
dna.default: topology=rhizome - the shipped network line for line. generate_primary_connections keeps the same three-nearest loop with the same randf() draw against the same branch_prob, generate_secondary_branches builds the same 250 nodes from the same three randf_range calls and hands over the same flat 0.7 width_multiplier, sever_network returns on its first line, and the seed ring keeps the identical layer_y expression. The tree, plateau and rupture code is reachable only from a non-default word, so the RNG consumes exactly the draws it always consumed in exactly the order it consumed them. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 14 mentions across 12 map files, not the 5 the promotion brief carried, and four reach-paths rather than one - bare tokens in PG_Mirrored_Patterns and its three parts and in ProceduralGeneration_Eight; a curation_station collection in Corridor_PG_Mirrored_Patterns whose #layout and #with_* flags belong to the station and not to this artifact; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:s#mount:rhizomatic_maze_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value; and `rhizomatic_maze_space->layered_membrane` in Trial_rooms_proceduralgeneration, which is a transformation target and not a config. Not one of the fourteen carries a topology key, and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names a word this file knows AND that word differs from the one it holds AND _ready has already grown the maze once.
dna.was: thirteen float and int exports, none of which said what the artifact is FOR. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS because nothing enumerated: branch_probability could be turned from 0.7 to 0.8 but there was no way for a map to ask for the thing the name promises. An artifact called rhizomatic shipped exactly one topology, and — measured rather than assumed — it was mostly a TREE: the only rhizomatic operation in the file is the three-nearest-neighbour pass over about 20 seeds, while the 250 secondary branches each attach by exactly one edge and close no loop at all.
dna.note: The axis is Deleuze and Guattari's own opposition, not a dial. `tree` is a minimum spanning tree from the lowest seed with growth oriented away from the root and tunnel width tapering by depth, so hierarchy is visible as thickness — there is no critically-rhizomatic middle value, the way bouncing_ball found there is no critically-bouncing. `severed` is asignifying rupture performed ON a finished rhizome rather than a different way of growing one, and it recounts node degrees afterwards so the chamber pass cannot drop a nine-metre CSG sphere into the fissure it just opened. `plateau` keeps every seed the four levels would have made and puts them all on one, so the comparison is about arrangement and not about how much was grown.
dna.declined: branch_probability, growth_iterations, merge_threshold, chamber_probability, organic_distortion and tunnel_segments — six knobs that are already exports and all of them decline for the same reason: they change how MUCH tangle there is, not what the tangle claims. connection_probability and deadend_pruning are declined for a different reason worth recording: they are exported, they are set in the .tscn, and no line of code reads either of them.
dna.still_note: topology is resolved before a single tunnel mesh is built and never moves again, so one frame is a complete account of it. Expect plateau to be the loudest value by far — a 25 m tower collapsing to a flat mat is a silhouette change, not a texture one. tree and rhizome differ in loop structure and in tunnel thickness rather than in extent, so compare where routes close and how width falls off toward the periphery.
dna.deepened_why: THE BENCH HAD NEVER PHOTOGRAPHED THIS ARTIFACT, and that is the finding — the axis was not on trial, it was never called. The sweep reported peak 0.062% across ALL SIX pairs on a subject of 8.217%, and the tell is that the peak was rhizome-vs-plateau, the pair the still_note above had predicted would be the loudest in the batch by a distance: a 25 m tower against a flat mat cannot differ by six hundredths of a percent. A number that impossible is a fact about the instrument. Three causes, all measured in the sheet at doc/reports/sweep_rhizomatic_maze_space.png rather than guessed: (1) the .tscn carries a DebugInfo Control — a 390x110 panel with a RichTextLabel reading 'Generating organic tunnel network...' — and the sweep's chrome suppressor stands down CanvasLayer and Camera3D only, so a Control under a Node3D drew straight into the viewport and IS the 8.2% subject, identical in every frame. The statistic that was supposed to report on the axis was mostly a photograph of a debug readout. (2) NavigationHelpers hangs four 0.6 m marker spheres at x,z = +/-25; they are MeshInstance3D, so they pin the fitted AABB to a 50 m box no matter what the maze does, which put the camera about 220 m out. (3) At 220 m the artifact's own WorldEnvironment — volumetric fog at density 0.03 over a 50 m length, authored for a player standing INSIDE the tunnels — fills the frame with haze: the background samples (130,165,118) and the 90th percentile of per-pixel difference from it is SEVEN grey levels. The maze is a ghost, and it visibly MOVES between the four tiles, which is the proof the values were arriving all along. Repair: a bench-only `bench_stage` export, the same shape as the existing layout_draw, defaulting to `scene`; `bare` frees the Control and the marker spheres and turns off exactly two properties on the environment (fog_enabled, volumetric_fog_enabled) rather than freeing it — with the sweep rig adding a WorldEnvironment of its own, two in a tree is undefined enough that freeing would make the picture depend on node order, and this scene's own 0.02/0.02/0.08 background is the best backdrop available for tunnels of albedo 0.7/0.8/0.9. It touches no generator code and no placement sets it. THE SECOND REPAIR IS THE DESIGN ONE and it stands on its own: severed cut the graph in half and left both halves where they were, measuring 0.012% against the intact rhizome. The tempting reading is the Deleuzian one — that cutting a rhizome changes nothing because any point still reaches any other — and it is wrong about this code: a plane cut removes EVERY crossing edge, so the graph really does fall into two components. The failure was that CONNECTION IS NOT A VISIBLE PROPERTY. The fissure is now 0.14 of maze_size.x instead of 0.08 and the two fragments stand 0.06 apart on each side, so the wound is about 20 m of a 50 m object and reads in the silhouette; tendrils are suppressed over the gap so nothing sews it shut. Extent grows about 12%, which the freed camera repays many times.
dna.expected: NO NUMBER IS PREDICTED HERE, and that is honest rather than evasive: nothing about this artifact has ever been photographed, so there is no scale to extrapolate from. What IS predicted is the SHAPE of the result, and it is falsifiable. (1) The frame should stop being a flat field: the background sampled at (3,3) should come back near (5,5,18) instead of (130,165,118), and the 90th percentile of per-pixel difference from it should rise from 7 grey levels into the dozens. (2) The loudest pair should become rhizome-vs-plateau, because a 25 m tower against a flat mat is a silhouette. (3) The subject share will probably FALL from 8.2%, and that is the fix working, not failing - the 8.2% was a debug panel that has now been freed, so the number will finally be about the maze. IF EVERY PAIR IS STILL UNDER 0.1%, the fixture did not arrive: check that bench_stage reached the root before concluding anything at all about topology.
dna.deepened_declined: A FIFTH VALUE, `radicle` — Deleuze and Guattari's own middle figure, the fascicular root whose principal root has aborted and onto which an indefinite multiplicity of secondary roots grafts. It is the strongest thing missing from this axis, because it is the figure that LOOKS tangled and still is not a rhizome, which is the distinction the whole Introduction turns on, and the axis currently ships the two easy poles and two operations. It is not taken in this pass on a sequencing judgement: not one of the four existing values has ever been photographed, so designing a fifth against an imagined frame is the finished-looking-experiment failure the promotion brief warns about — 'an artifact that does not build is a finding, not an axis' applies just as well to an artifact that has never been seen. Take it after a clean sweep exists. Implementation sketch so the next agent does not start cold: connect_as_radicle() builds a short thick taproot from the lowest seed to a graft node above it, joins every other seed to that ONE graft at equal width (the star, against tree's spanning chain), and generate_secondary_branches concentrates the flourish near the graft with NO taper, because in a radicle the unity is the pivot and not the branching. The 20 primary connections are only about 16% of the 270 the file builds, so the secondary rule has to carry the value too or it will read as a variation on tree.
dna.open: THE SAME THREE CHILDREN SHIP INTO EVERY MAP, and this is NOT repaired here. All fourteen placements get the DebugInfo Control — a panel reading 'Generating organic tunnel network...' with the parameter list under it — because neither the sweep's chrome suppressor nor GridInteractablesComponent._suppress_embedded_chrome stands down a raw Control, and a Control under a Node3D draws to the viewport regardless. They also get a WorldEnvironment that overrides the map's own environment with volumetric fog, and four navigation marker spheres at +/-25 m that inflate the AABB the grid auto-grounds against. Every one of those is a change to what fourteen rooms look like, so fixing it belongs in its own pass with its own walk, not smuggled in under a DNA deepening. Worth checking how many other artifacts carry a Control child before repairing this one alone — the suppressor is the shared meeting point and this is likely a class, not a case.

rhizomatic_maze_space.description: A labyrinthine exploration of rhizomatic growth patterns, creating interconnected maze-like spaces that grow organically like fungal networks or plant root systems
rhizomatic_maze_space.name: Rhizomatic Maze Space
rhizomatic_maze_space.qfep_connection: A labyrinth grown as rhizome — interconnected, centerless, any point reachable from any other by more than one route. The counter-maze: where recursive backtracking makes a tree with a single path, this makes a mesh with many, Deleuze's figure walked as architecture. A world with no author and, deliberately, no throughline either.

rhizomatic_structure.description: Grow a network that refuses root, trunk, and leaves. Recursive branching creates a scaffold, then lateral reconnections turn that scaffold into a mesh where any point can connect to any other. Adjusting reconnection probability moves the artifact between tree and rhizome, making hierarchy versus multiplicity a concrete topological choice. It brings Deleuze and Guattari into graph theory by questioning when a tree is the wrong model.
rhizomatic_structure.name: Rhizomatic Structure
rhizomatic_structure.qfep_connection: A challenge to hierarchical F: lateral reconnection redistributes structure away from roots and trunks. It asks what graph order looks like when no center is privileged.
rhizomatic_structure.gamwell_reference: Non-Euclidean geometry, Riemannian manifolds, topology, rhizome theory (Deleuze & Guattari), spatial perception
rhizomatic_structure.capacity: COMPARE tree-like and rhizomatic topologies by tuning how often local branches reconnect laterally.
interactions: tune connection_probability to move between tree and rhizome
inspect cycles formed by lateral reconnections

riemann_pi.name: riemann_pi
riemann_pi.qfep_connection: integration: pi estimated by Riemann slices — the circle's area approached rectangle by rectangle; the constant everyone knows, earned the slow way. Accumulation auditioning for exactness.

riemann_sphere.description: The Riemann sphere — compactified complex plane with stereographic projection lines, north pole at infinity, equator, and projection plane visible.
riemann_sphere.name: Riemann Sphere

triangle_curvature_workbench.name: Triangle Curvature Workbench
triangle_curvature_workbench.description: An interactive workbench for Gauss-Bonnet on a triangle. One slider drives Gaussian curvature K through seven detents {-2, -1, -0.5, 0, +0.5, +1, +2}; the host surface morphs with K's sign (Poincaré disk for K<0, flat cyan grid for K=0, violet sphere for K>0); three triangle vertices at canonical 30° geodesic separation stay fixed while their connecting edges become geodesics ON the active surface (arcs, lines, great-circle arcs); the readout shows α + β + γ in degrees, the Gauss-Bonnet excess (sphere) or defect (disk) as a signed angle, and a regime word. The slider IS Gauss-Bonnet — the parallel postulate exposed as a setting on K, not a truth about lines. Paired with /triangle-table-gallery's nine cells (3 surfaces × 3 sizes).
triangle_curvature_workbench.capacity: WALK Gauss-Bonnet — angle sum is a property of the surface

riemann_torus.name: riemann_torus
riemann_torus.qfep_connection: Drag two lattice vectors on the floor and the label recomputes τ = ω₂/ω₁ live: every torus is the same plane under a different quotient, and the shape you took for a doughnut turns out to be the ratio of two arrows.
